objective: Bound the evaluation matrix before any run starts: cap versions, scenarios and their product, refuse an oversized matrix with an actionable message, and offer a dry-run count.
decision_supported: Can --versions and --scenarios stay unbounded, or does the product need an explicit budget before the first external process starts?
acceptance: A matrix over the run limit is refused before any run starts.
More versions or scenarios than the per-list limits is refused.
The refusal names every problem at once and says how to proceed.
--dry-run reports the matrix size and starts nothing.
A dry run over the limit still refuses.
sim_cli.run_scenarios applies the same per-invocation scenario ceiling.
evidence: Before the change the module had MAX_EVENT_LOG_BYTES and MAX_EVENTS_PER_RUN but no limit on the number of runs, so 50 versions x 50 scenarios would have started 2500 runs.
After the change the same input is refused with '50 versions, over the 20-version limit; 50 scenarios, over the 50-scenario limit; 2500 runs, over the 100-run limit'.
A 2x3 matrix reports 6 runs and is accepted; the exact limits are accepted.
--dry-run prints '2 version(s) x 1 scenario(s) = 2 run(s)' and returns 0 without creating the output directory.
stop_conditions: A legitimate evaluation needs more than 100 runs in one invocation; the limits are three constants at the top of the module and the message says to split the work.
risks_and_fallbacks: The limits are guesses sized well above any committed corpus; they live in one place so a reviewer can raise them deliberately.
The product limit is checked separately from the per-list limits so a 20x50 matrix is refused for its product even though each list is at its own ceiling.
